defects: The camera stays locked off on one static harbour plate for the whole 20 s. The only movement is word-by-word blur/fade reveals and the city lights switching off, so most seconds play as dead air.
Every line uses the same blur-to-sharp reveal and blur-out exit, with no variation in spacing, scale or position. One move repeats for every line.
The harbour lights go out as a hard state change between lines (lit at line 2, dark by line 3). They do not die out one by one, so the film's central event plays without timing.
The type's reflection in the water is a flat vertical flip with uniform blur. It has no ripple distortion, so it reads as a 2D layer laid over the scene rather than light on water.
The water ripples and light reflections are evenly spaced procedural streaks, and the buildings are flat block silhouettes. At 100% this looks generated rather than art-directed.
Mid-reveal frames carry half-blurred words, so several sampled frames do not hold up as posters.
Text sits in the same top-left slot every time, with no layout change across lines.
gaps: Choreography: the film needs camera life (a slow push or a drift at the tide line) and a sequenced, overlapping die-off of the harbour lights timed to the lyric. As built, it is a static plate with one reveal effect.

Arc and pace: energy is flat from start to end. Nothing builds to a peak at 60-80%, and the single cut does not land on anything. Top work would turn the lights going out into the climax and give the 'but we stayed on' beat a real hold and release.

Finish and sync: the scene needs real water interaction for the reflections, more material detail in the skyline and boat, and word reveals locked to the visible piano/vocal onsets in the spectrogram (bursts near 2.4 s, 7 s and 16 s). The track is a sparse, produced keys bed with some dynamics, but the picture does not visibly answer it.
